text:
A: Hello! Nasreen, yeah? Tomasz. You can hear me?
B: Yes, hello. I can hear you.
A: Perfect. Third one, eh? I'm getting good at this. So what do you do, Nasreen?
B: Erm, I'm between jobs at the moment. Before I was receptionist, at a GP surgery in Walsall.
A: Okay. Receptionist. And now you're looking for something?
B: Yes, maybe part-time. When, you know, when things are settled.
A: Mm. To be fair, reception is basically sales. You deal with angry people, you make them feel okay. Same thing I do, just I get commission.
B: Ha, yes. Nobody gave me commission.
A: That's the problem, see. I sell cars, premium German, in Park Royal. Saturday I sold three. You keep people happy, they sign. Simple.
B: Three in one day? That's very good.
A: It was good day. One finance deal still waiting, bank is slow. So, Walsall. You have family there?
B: My partner and my son. My son is seventeen. And my daughter is in Birmingham.
A: Seventeen, okay. My sister has kids, they're little, crazy, always on the iPad.
B: Same. Zain is always on the phone. And the fridge.
A: Ha. Where's your family from originally? If you don't mind.
B: Pakistan. Mirpur. I came here when I was twenty-one.
A: Twenty-one! I came at twenty-two. From Poland, Wrocław. 2008.
B: Oh, acha. So we are both, you know, came here young.
A: Exactly. I came for one year, to make money. Sixteen years later, still here. Your mum is still back there?
B: Yes. She's getting old now. I talk to her on WhatsApp every day.
A: My mum is the same, but she sends me photo of her dog. Every day, mate, every single day. Same dog, same sofa.
B: That's nice, though. She misses you.
A: Yeah. Yeah, I know. I go back two, three times a year. You go back much?
B: Not since before COVID. It's expensive, and, erm, the flight is long. I would like to do Umrah also, one day.
A: Umrah, that's Mecca, yeah? My colleague went. He said hotel was amazing, five star, view of everything.
B: Some are very nice, yes. Very expensive, though.
A: Everything good is expensive. That's what I tell my customers. So, er, the puzzle, you finished it?
B: Not all. The shapes one.
A: Everybody says shapes. I think they made it hard on purpose.
B: Maybe. You know, you remind me a bit of my cousin's husband. He also talks very fast.
A: Is he selling something?
B: Mobile phones. In a shop on Soho Road.
A: Ha! See, I knew. Salesman recognises salesman. Tell him if he wants to sell cars—
